prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished design exploration board for StarlitCoffee, an Android coffee brewing app. This is a proposal, not an implemented screen.
Composition: landscape board with exactly TWO tall Android screen designs side by side, both entire screen visible with clean straight edges, no hardware bezel, no perspective. Large readable typography, practical 48dp touch targets, no cropped content or overlapping footer. Small board title above. LEFT is short brew ready to begin bloom; RIGHT is cold brew already steeping. These are separate methods, NOT simultaneously active sessions.
Same example content for fair comparison:
LEFT app header "Pulsar". Recipe facts "30 g coffee", "510 g total water", "93–96 °C". Current instruction "Pour 90 g bloom water" and "Close valve". Timer ready "00:00". One single dominant action "Start bloom", secondary text action "Finish brew". Next stage is "Next · Main pour". Always distinguish bloom amount from TOTAL recipe water. NO live scale measurement; do not imply Bluetooth or connected kettle. No duplicate play control. Guidance can be reached via a discreet "Details" disclosure.
RIGHT header "Cold brew"; state "Steeping"; "1 h 22 m" labeled "Elapsed"; "12 h 37 m" labeled "Until reminder". "Edit reminder" as compact secondary action. Reminder permission issue is an amber compact actionable row "Precise reminders off" with "Enable", visually separate from storage guidance. Visible compact storage cue "Keep covered at 4 °C or colder" with "Storage guidance" disclosure; no giant red warning unless actual urgent hazard. A "Finish brew" action and normal Back navigation. Waiting is visually relaxed, never a fake one-step wizard. No pause cold-brew-time control.
Avoid dashboards unrelated to brewing, charts of invented measurements, social features, badges, subscriptions, extraneous settings, paragraphs of boilerplate, coffee emoji buttons, low contrast, excessive whitespace that crowds controls. Natural simple English. Crisp high fidelity native app UI, precise layout.
Board title "01 / FOCUS".
Design direction: Evolution of the old quiet timer. Midnight charcoal background, warm off-white typography, restrained lilac primary action. No card stack. Extremely clear dominant current action/quantity with tabular timer, compact recipe line, minimal thin separators. LEFT small refined existing-coffee-bean-inspired illustration near top (not enormous), then hero "90 g" labeled "Bloom water", instruction beneath, 00:00 timer secondary, compact Next line and Details, one broad lilac Start bloom near bottom. RIGHT hero elapsed clock, calm Steeping label, until-reminder secondary, compact two support rows, modest outlined Finish brew. Layout feels resolved and balanced rather than empty. Minimalism is about the hierarchy, not hiding essentials.
